c145.title: A Day at the Port
c145.story: On Saturday, Max visited his uncle Petro at the [[port]] of Odesa. A big ship was waiting in the [[dock]] for repairs. Next to it, an empty oil [[tanker]] carried only seawater as [[ballast]]. "That ship brings oil, and a [[barrel]] costs more every month," his uncle said. In the warehouse, boxes of [[cargo]] moved slowly along a [[conveyor]]. "Grain is our main [[export]], and this coffee is an [[import]] from South America," he explained. "So I am an [[exporter]] and an [[importer]] at the same time." Max asked why the coffee was so expensive. "New [[tariffs|tariff]] on coffee, and each company has a yearly [[quota]] too," Uncle Petro sighed. Then a rich [[industrialist]] in a gray suit arrived at the office. He wanted to start a [[joint venture]] with Max's uncle. That evening, Max told Anna he might study business after all.

c146.title: Uncle Oleh, the Trader
c146.story: Anna's uncle Oleh works as a [[trader]] at a big bank in Kyiv. At Sunday lunch, Anna asked him what [[trading]] really is. "I buy and sell shares for people, a bit like a [[broker]]," he said. "You can open your own account at a [[brokerage]] with very little money." He showed her the stock market [[index]] on his phone. "This company pays me a [[dividend]] every quarter," he smiled. Then he admitted that he also bought some [[bitcoin]] last year. "Most people just try to follow the [[smart money]]," he added. He also explained oil [[futures]] and a strange [[derivative]] that nobody at the table understood. His old friend now runs a [[hedge fund]] in London. Anna laughed and said she would study [[asset management]], starting with her pocket money.

c147.title: Buying a New Flat
c147.story: Anna's parents finally decided to buy a new flat. A local [[developer]] is building the house, and a [[consortium]] of banks is paying for it. It will be a modern [[condominium]] with a small park and a playground. Anna's mother, who works in [[banking]], quickly found them a good loan. The loan even has a six-month [[grace period]] before the first payment. Their money will stay in [[escrow]] until the flat is ready. The bank, as their [[creditor]], checked how much money they keep in [[reserve]]. The city also gave them a small [[rebate]] for choosing an energy-saving home. Anna's father still worried, so he called his friend, an [[auditor]]. She said the building company had a clean [[audit]] last year. That night, the whole family looked at the plans and chose Anna's future room.

c148.title: The Economy on TV
c148.story: Anna and Max were watching the evening news at Max's flat. An [[economist]] in a blue jacket talked about a [[boom]] in online shopping. "But some small shops are close to [[collapse]]," she warned. Then she explained what a budget [[deficit]] is, using a simple chart. "Some countries owe more than a [[trillion]] dollars," she said. Max's grandpa laughed and took an old [[ruble]] coin out of his pocket. "When a country cannot pay its debts, we call it [[default]]," the economist continued. Next, a bank [[insider]] told reporters how a drug [[cartel]] tried to hide its money. Thanks to good [[risk management]], the bank stopped them in time. After that, a [[broker-dealer]] gave tips about buying and selling stocks. Anna yawned and changed the channel to an ad for [[tax-free]] shopping at the airport. "That's the only economy I understand," Max joked.

c149.title: A Party for the Rich
c149.story: Max's rich cousin Denys invited him to a [[cocktail party]] in a fancy hotel. The evening started with a funny old-style [[burlesque]] show with songs and jokes. Denys introduced Max to a [[self-made]] businessman from a small village. The man became a [[millionaire]] before he turned thirty. Next to him stood an oil [[magnate]] who owned a huge [[conglomerate]]. "I have [[business interests|business interest]] in five countries," he told Max proudly. A group of actors from [[show business]] were discussing their new movie. "It did great at the [[box office]]," one actress said, eating [[caviar]] on tiny crackers. Later, a quiet old man gave a big [[endowment]] to the university where Max studies. Max decided that was the most impressive thing he saw all night.

c150.title: Consultants at the Office
c150.story: On Monday, a [[consultant]] named Laura arrived at Max's company. She works in [[consulting]] and visits a new company every month. She invited everyone to a hall in the [[business center]] for a [[workshop]]. First, she talked about [[project management]] and how to plan tasks better. Then she discussed [[recruiting]] and how to find talented young people. After lunch, she wrote a long [[memorandum]] for the company's [[directorate]]. It also gave advice about working with clients in [[pharma]]. Max helped her put boxes of old papers into the [[shredder]]. The company even sold its old furniture at an [[auction]]. Every [[middle manager]] in the office was worried about their job. But on Friday, Laura said the team was doing great, and everyone finally relaxed.

c151.title: A Meeting at City Hall
c151.story: On Tuesday evening, Anna and Max went to a meeting at city hall about their street. On the wall hung a painting of an old [[prefect]] who ruled for an emperor. The [[mayor]] and a local [[alderman]] sat under it and opened the meeting. First, they talked about new [[zoning]] rules and modern [[urban design]]. "We want Kyiv to become a [[smart city]] with apps and sensors," she said. A tired [[bureaucrat]] showed everyone a pile of papers and maps. Then the neighbors got angry. "A [[bulldozer]] will destroy our [[community center]]!" one woman shouted. Others worried about the old [[kiosk]], the [[barbershop]] and the bus [[depot]]. "Some [[squatters|squatter]] live there now, and they need help," an old man added. Finally, the city leaders promised to save the places people loved, and everyone clapped.

c152.title: Anna Volunteers
c152.story: This autumn, Anna became a [[volunteer]] at a small [[charity]] in Kyiv. Her boss, Iryna, is a professional [[fundraiser]] with endless energy. Together they do [[fundraising]] for war [[veterans|veteran]] and their families. They also collect money for a little boy with [[lymphoma]]. The charity does [[advocacy]] for old people who live like [[paupers|pauper]] in cold houses. On Saturday, Anna sold forty [[handmade]] cards at the market. After that, she laid flowers at the war [[memorial]] in the park. She thought about the soldiers' [[heroism]] and felt quiet [[patriotism]] in her heart. Then Iryna called with good news: the boy's family now had enough money for treatment.

c153.title: The New Neighbors
c153.story: A family of [[immigrants|immigrant]] moved into Anna's building last week. Their son lives in America and just got his [[green card]]. Last month, their daughter Lina visited the [[consulate]], where the [[consul]] helped her. Lina told Anna about [[racism]] at her old school and a [[racist]] neighbor there. Before Kyiv, the family lived in a poor [[ghetto]] in a big, noisy city. Now her parents work hard and hope to join the [[middle class]] here. Anna's grandpa was born in the [[baby boom]], so he is a real [[baby boomer]]. He calls himself a [[nationalist]], so Lina asked him what that means. They had a long but friendly argument about [[nationalism]]. In the end, Grandpa smiled and said, "Every [[migrant]] is welcome at my table."

c154.title: Election Night Drama
c154.story: On Sunday night, Anna and Max watched the last episode of their favorite political drama. In the show, a national [[broadcaster]] covers election night in an imaginary country. The old [[president]] and his [[vice president]] wait nervously in their office. Each [[candidate]] gives a speech: a [[democrat]], a [[liberal]] and a [[social democrat]]. They all say they understand the [[electorate]] and want a strong [[mandate]]. Earlier in the season, Max got confused about the [[primaries]] and the [[caucus]]. Anna explained them, and also the [[referendum]] from episode three. A funny British guest, a [[Tory]], keeps comparing everything to London. Outside, a crowd of [[loyalists|loyalist]] waves flags for the old leader. In the end, a young woman with lots of [[charisma]] wins. Max clapped and asked, "Can we watch the next season tomorrow?"

c155.title: A Day in Parliament
c155.story: On Thursday, Anna's class went on a school trip to [[parliament]]. A friendly guide explained that every party has its own political [[agenda]]. First, they watched a short press [[briefing]] in a bright hall. A young [[minister]] spoke about new schools, and then the [[premier]] talked about the budget. Mr. Koval explained that some countries have a [[senate]], where each [[senator]] votes on laws. In the hall, a [[lobbyist]] from the energy [[lobby]] waited with a thick folder. The members argued for hours but finally reached a [[compromise]]. The guide said full [[consensus]] is rare, because many people just want the [[status quo]]. Now they had a budget, so there would be no [[shutdown]] this year. Anna asked about [[impeachment]], and Mr. Koval explained it with a funny example. On the bus home, Max asked so many questions that he became the [[de facto]] guide.

c156.title: A Summit in Geneva
c156.story: Last week, Anna's aunt Olena worked as an interpreter at a [[summit]] in Geneva. On the first morning, she picked up her badge at the [[secretariat]] on the second floor. The hall was full of [[diplomats|diplomat]] and nervous [[delegates|delegate]] from many countries. Each [[bloc]] wanted to build a stronger [[alliance]] with its neighbors. On the second day, two small countries signed a peace [[pact]]. They also talked about ending an [[embargo]] on fruit and grain. One leader threatened to use his [[veto]], but in the end he agreed. An [[emir]] in white robes gave a short, warm speech. Then the elderly [[sovereign]] of a tiny island kingdom spoke about the ocean. An American [[congressman]] and a [[congresswoman]] from the same state spoke too. Olena translated every word without a single mistake. "Next month, a medical [[congress]] will feel easy," she told Anna that night.
